title: Express Language Modeling
claim: Our approximation gives much larger speed-ups than prior fast methods at better accuracy, with error that stays bounded as length grows.
layout: 4 panels in 2x2 grid, line plots, shared color legend across panels
description: A 2x2 grid of line plots, each with a bold panel title. (a) Masked prefill: speed-up over FlashAttention 2 against sequence length from 32k to 512k. The blue Thinformer Express (h=9) line climbs steeply to about 60x. The green h=10 line reaches about 30x. The orange HyperAttention line stops near 13x at 256k. (b) Relative perplexity against runtime in ms at n=32768, with a dashed grey 'Exact' line at 1.00. The Express curves lie at or below the orange HyperAttention curve. (c) Approximation error against token position on a log scale. Four shaded curves for h=7 to 10 jump from zero, then stay flat and bounded and drop as h grows. (d) Unmasked prefill speed-up for Thinformer Triton (solid blue) against Original (dashed red). Triton reaches about 32x and Original about 15x. The eye goes first to the steep blue line in (a).
caption: Accelerating long-context prefill. For masked attention, Thinformer Express attains larger speed-ups over FlashAttention 2 than the Triton HyperAttention algorithm (a) while improving the runtime-perplexity trade-off on LongBench-E tasks (b). (c) As predicted by Thm. 3, the scaled Thinformer Express attention approximation error ∥bon −on∥∞/√log n log log n remains bounded for all n and decays with increasing cache size nout = 2h. (d) For unmasked attention, our I/O-aware Triton implementation also provides speed-ups over the original Torch-compiled Thinformer.
abstract: We introduce a new tool, Express, for converting a non-causal attention approximation into a causal approximation with matching approximation guarantees. When combined with the state-of-the-art Thinformer approximation, Express improves upon the best known causal attention guarantees, delivering $\log^{3/2}(n)/s$ approximation error with only $O(s)$ memory and $O(s^2 \log^2(n))$ compression overhead for a sequence of length $n$. We pair these developments with an efficient I/O-aware Triton implementation, demonstrate substantial speedups over FlashAttention 2, and use Express to overcome four resource bottlenecks in the language modeling pipeline: long-context prefill, KV cache compression, long-form memory-constrained decoding, and long-form compute-constrained decoding.
